newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices jump on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices jump on cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices kept climbing on Wednesday as cold weather blanketed most market areas and volumes were withdrawn from storage just to meet pipeline load targets, trading sources said.
"Prices are rocking and rolling," one Calgary-based marketer said.

Cold weather and high demand at Empress, Alberta, where TransCanada PipeLines Ltd. takes gas to ship to eastern Canadian and U.S. Midwest markets, forced the withdrawal on Tuesday of 240 million cubic feet per day from Alberta facilities when injections should be at high levels, he said.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub was quoted at C$1.89 per gigigajoule, up about five cents from Tuesday and 16 cents from last Wednesday. May AECO was quoted at C$1.74/1.75 per GJ, up from C$1.68 last week.
More cold weather and snow rolled into western Canada this week and temperatures in Alberta were not expected to climb above freezing until at least Friday, Environment Canada said.
The marketer said he estimated about 600 million cubic feet would have to be injected into western Canadian storage each day through October to meet expected demand for the upcoming heating season.
"The only thing positive is a warming up on the weekend, but I don't know if that matters," he said.

At the borders, prices for gas destined to U.S. Midwest markets were up about US25 cents per million British thermal units from last week as cold weather continued in most of the region, traders said.
Gas at Niagara in southern Ontario rose about US30 cents on the week into the mid-US$2.30s per mmBtu.
